AGENDA ITEMS AND ACTIONS
5:00 P.M. CLOSED SESSION

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Mendoza called meeting to order at 5:04 p.m. via teleconferencing.    

ROLL CALL

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION ITEMS There were no individuals wishing to address the City Council on any items on Closed Session agenda.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION The City Council/Successor Agency recessed to Closed Session at 5:05 p.m.

RECONVENE TO OPEN SESSION The City Council/Successor Agency reconvened to Open Session at 6:09 p.m. via teleconferencing. 

ORAL CLOSED SESSION ANNOUNCEMENT City Attorney Tapia reported on Closed Session items: 

Items #1, #2, #3, and #4  - Staff made presentation, the City Council provided feedback, and no reportable action was taken on these items.  

Item #5 - The City Council discussed only one matter.  Staff made presentation, the City Council provided feedback, and no reportable action was taken on this item.

6:00 P.M. - CITY COUNCIL MEETING

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Mendoza called regular City Council meeting to order.  

ROLL CALL

APPEARANCES AND PRESENTATIONS

1.. Presentation/Update from the Sheriff's Department Regarding Public Safety in the City of Commerce Sgt. Villarreal provided an update for the last two weeks. According to Sergeant Villarreal, Deputies attended two Neighborhood Watch meetings -one in the Village and the other on Jardine and Strong. 

Councilmember Altamirano thanked Deputies who apprehended the person trying to set the building on fire on Telegraph and how professionally everyone responded and made an arrest. Councilmember Argumedo also commended Deputies for resent arrest made in murder suspect. 



2.. Proclamation Designating March 21, 2022 as Down Syndrome Awareness Day Mayor Mendoza read the proclamation. Social Services Coordinator Garcia showed a video regarding down syndrome, and Susana Cisneros, Special Needs Commissioner, thanked the City Council for celebrating and bringing awareness to down syndrome. Commissioner Cisneros Invited everyone to attend the Walk on Water Surf Therapy event in Ventura on March 26th. Councilmembers, Mayor Pro Tem, and Mayor thanked Ms. Cisneros for all efforts, advocating and being an advocate for creating Social Needs Commission. 

PUBLIC COMMENT Edna Jimenez, the Outreach Consultant for Metro, spoke regarding Metro efforts to extend for Atlantic and Pomona in East Los Angeles and stated that the environmental report is almost ready. Ms. Jimenez announced upcoming community meetings. 

Director of Administrative Services and City Clerk Shumway read a comment from Kevin Larsen, President of Local AFSCME 775, urging the Council to fill positions in the Transportation Department and eliminate the pay cut that employees took during the pandemic. 





CONSENT CALENDAR  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Oralia Rebollo

7.. Annual Comprehensive Financial Report for Fiscal Year Ended June 30, 2021

5.. Approval of Minutes

8.. Authorize Acceptance of Clean California Local Grant Program Grant

6.. Re-Ratifying the Proclamation of a State of Emergency by Governor Newsom, and Re-Authorizing Remote Teleconference Meetings of the Legislative Bodies of the City of Commerce for the 30-Day Period

4.. Approval of Warrant Register Nos. 14A, & 14B

12.. Denial of Speed Hump Installation Request Pursuant to Speed Hump Policy  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Oralia Rebollo Director of Public Works Hernandez provided an overview of the staff report. 

Discussion took place. Mayor Pro Tem Rebollo recommended that staff assists with getting two more signatures and re-access t the application. Mayor Mendoza stated that all streets around have speed humps, needing them in that area. Director Hernandez explained that the denial is based on approved policy and engineering criteria, and in addition, not all residents are in support of speed humps. 

Mayor Mendoza made motion to approve the speed humps. Motion died for the lack of a second. Councilmember Argumedo recommended that staff looks at the application and bring this application for discussion at a future meeting. 





SCHEDULED MATTERS

10.. Formation of Underground Utilities District No 22-1 for Harbor Street from Commerce Way to Eastern Avenue  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Hugo Argumedo Director of Public Works Hernandez provided an overview of the staff report. 
Discussion took place regarding the impacts of this project on the area, and specifically on school. It was stated that impact would be minimized, and the street would not close. Councilmember Altamirano suggested creating art for that wall in the Village, and Mayor Mendoza recommended the installation of solar light polls as well as including wifi and making poles higher to accommodate the banner program. 

Mayor Mendoza opened Public Hearing. There were no individuals wishing to address the City Council on this item. Mayor Mendoza closed Public Hearing.


11.. Mid-Year Budget Review - Amending the Annual Operating and Capital Budgets for Fiscal Year 2021-2022  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Oralia Rebollo Finance Director Brooks brook provided an overview of the staff report.  According to Director Brooks, the revenues are almost back to what it was before, and that means that the City could go to Option B, which allows two million in additional revenues.  

Mayor Mendoza recommended that line by line recommended adjustments or requests be sent ahead of time for the City Council review.   

ORDINANCES

9.. First Reading of Uncodified Ordinance Approving a Development Agreement Related to Application #18-026  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Hugo Argumedo Director of Planning and Economic Development Jimenez provided an overview of the staff report.

CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS City Manager Cisneros stated that Councilmember Altamirano is having technical issues. On his behalf, he asked that staff provide an update on re-opening City's gym and requested that seniors be allowed to use Senior Center or use EOC. Councilmember Altamirano extended his prayer for people in Ukraine and wished all women Happy International Women's Day. 

Councilmember Argumedo stated that he attended two Neighborhood Watch meetings and asked that the report be provided back on addressing issues brought up at the meetings. 

Mayor Pro Tem Rebollo wished all women Happy International Women's Day. 

Mayor Mendoza reported that he attended the Neighborhood Watch at Pueblo Court on February 24, attended Mary Youngs' 100-year birthday celebration on February 25, Neighborhood Watch meeting on Jardine and Strong on March 3, 2022, dinner at Steven's Steakhouse with Mr. Cervantes, and participated in scholarship program events at St. Marcelina's church on February 26, 2022. 

Mayor Mendoza requested a Resolution to stand together with Ukraine.

PUBLIC HEARING

3.. Transportation Informational Session Mayor Mendoza spoke about the high volume of phone calls regarding recent changes to transportation routes. There should have placed a pilot program before implementation. According to Mayor Mendoza, while implementing faster routes, buses are driving empty. City Manager Cisneros stated that staff would bring an interim update on the City Council meeting on March 22, 2022. 

Director of Transportation McFerguson stated that staff conducted a survey and received 175 surveys. As for Dial-A-Ride, seniors should be able to schedule a ride instead of waiting for the buses. According to Mayor Pro Tem Rebollo, she received only one complaint about morning school buses, and that issue was fixed. As for the Dial-A-Ride, concerns are mainly regarding the pick-up window and lack of flexibility of being dropped at other locations. Most of the people are just confused with the new routes; however, students are excited to be able to ride to Cal State LA. According to Director McFerguson, as for some of the smaller ridership and school drop-offs, the staff is proposing a microbus to accommodate those individuals. 

Discussion took place on whether some routes could be reinstated. 

Councilmember Soria recommended the workshop to decide whether keep the Commerce in Motion or go back to previous routes and also asked to compare ridership before COVID and now. 

Mayor Mendoza went over routes put in place and suggested that instead of waiting for 15 minutes at the hub, use that time to increase the routes with additional stops. Mayor Mendoza asked to place correct signage for bus stops and install a sign for the transportation hub. 

Jose Castillo stated that they would accommodate seniors and bring them to multiple destinations. According to Mr. Castillo, 15 minutes at the bus hub are dedicated for the buses to get on time as they sometimes get delayed at the routes.
